maria: Hey — I ran a combined nsys timeline + perf/flamegraph pass on the canary that showed the perf regression. GPU kernels look identical, but CPU-side time jumped and flamegraphs point to Python scheduler + tokenization hot paths.
jamal: ugh. quick numbers?
maria: baseline CPU user time ~120ms/sample, regressed ~220ms/sample. perf top shows heavy PyEval_EvalFrame and a spin in BatchCoordinator::wait_for_work.
eva: any syscall stalls (futex, epoll) in the timeline?
maria: yes — nsys timeline has frequent futex_wait and short wakeups around the batch boundary. looks like tight locking around enqueue/dequeue.
simon: can you paste the perf collapsed stacks you used for the flame?
maria: sure — this is a trimmed stackcollapse output from perf script + stackcollapse-perf.pl:
```
PyEval_EvalFrameEx;py_tokenize:100;BatchCoordinator::dispatch;pthread_mutex_lock;futex_wait  182
PyGILState_Ensure;py_tokenize;Batcher::enqueue;spin_read_lock;cpu_relax      98
PyEval_EvalFrameEx;KVCache::lookup;py_kv_miss;Batcher::assemble;pthread_cond_wait  72
```
jamal: interesting that KVCache lookup shows up. could be contention on a shared LRU or stats collection.
eva: did you capture native stacks for the C++ bits? which kernel selection functions?
maria: yes — most C++ time is in Batcher::enqueue/dispatch and small hot spots in KernelSelector::choose_variant at the moment we hit sequence-length edge cases. nothing huge there.
perf-bot: perf record command used: `sudo perf record -F 200 -g --pid 14523 -- sleep 60` then `perf script | ./stackcollapse-perf.pl > out.folded`
ben: any signs of GC thrash? python GC can show up as PyEval spikes and short pauses.
maria: good call — enabling tracemalloc + gc debug showed increased allocation churn for tokenization path on very short inputs after the change. GC collections per sec doubled.
simon: could be that we accidentally switched to a Python-level tokenizer fallback for some input shapes. Are we still using the C++ tokenizer for streaming requests?
maria: in the change that landed last week there's a path that falls back to the python tokenizer on malformed utf-8. the canary had a few malformed-ish prompts causing fallbacks.\ejam: (typo) — ignore
jamal: ok, remediation options: 1) avoid fallback in hot path (validate earlier/parsing layer), 2) move tokenization to worker pool native extension, 3) reduce locking granularity on Batcher queue (per-worker queues + work-stealing).
eva: also consider deferring stats/metrics aggregation off the critical path — we saw a small but measurable cost from atomic counters in KVCache::record_hit.
maria: small repro commands:
```
# run canary workload, capture perf
wrk -t4 -c128 -d60 http://localhost:8080/generate --script canary.lua
sudo perf record -F 200 -g --pid $(pgrep -f "redwood-runtime") -- sleep 60
```
jamal: for quick mitigation canary patch: change tokenizer fallback to queue into async-worker threadpool instead of executing inline. cheap and low-risk.
ben: +1. we should also add a perf/regression probe to CI that runs short flame/profile on tokenization-heavy trace.
maria: agreed — I'll open a PR with two things: move fallback off main thread, and add a perf smokecheck job. will also add a note to the rollout to watch futex wakeups in nsys.
simon: awesome. once PR is up ping me and I'll run the perf + nsys on the internal perf rig.
maria: thanks — attaching a small snapshot (pasted stacks above) and I'll follow up with the trace links in the thread after uploads finish. :thumbsup:
